newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close off highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close off highs.

text.p: French shares closed just inside positive territory as profit-taking ahead of Friday's monthly settlement knocked them from their best levels, dealers said.
Wall Street's sell-off also hit sentiment.
Volume was a heavy 6.1 billion francs.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 0.18 points or 0.01 percent higher at 2,233.57 while the CAC-40 futures contract settled 1.0 point lower at 2,238.0.
Dealers said the market was nervous and added further weakness could be expected with Friday's monthly settlement. The dollar's weakness could also weigh.

Some analysts said the French market was starting to look fairly valued to expensive and that investors were scrambling for new impetus to buy. In addition, some were starting to get worried about Wall Street, believing it was ripe for a correction. "We've got to get increasingly cautious with New York," said one trader, attributing its gravity-defying performance of late to year end "window dressing".
* Club Med up 3.08 percent, adding to recent gains on market talk leisure group Accor could launch a bid for the travel firm. Accor off 0.45 percent.

* Moulinex jumped early in the day after companies controlled by Hungarian-born investor George Soros bought 5.5 percent of the troubled French appliance maker but then retraced much of its gains to close up 1.26 percent. Appliance maker SEB was the big winner from Soros's move, finishing up 2.39 percent.
"Seb is up because people feel it has better fundamentals (than Moulinex)," said one trader.

* Rhone-Poulenc up 1.78 percent in volume of 2.60 million shares amid renewed market talk of an alliance between Rhone-Poulenc Rorer and Elf pharmaceutical unit Sanofi. Rhone's volume was swelled by a block trade of 610,000 shares at 160 francs per share at 1452 GMT. Elf gained 1.15 percent.

* Reinsurer Scor down 2.58 percent. It said its insurance costs totalling several million francs from Monday's fire in the Eurotunnel cross-Channel rail tunnel would have no impact on its 1996 result.

* Eurotunnel up 2.01 percent after recent heavy losses following Monday's Channel Tunnel fire. The tunnel reopened for limited business early Thursday and Eurotunnel said it hoped to start gradually reintroducing full service over next few days.

* UAP up 1.62 percent on volume of 5.46 million shares. Twenty-day exchange offer period opens under Axa merger plan. Axa up 1.69 percent. Salomon Brothers downgraded Axa to hold from buy in wake of the merger plan, saying it remained to be convinced that the insurer had made "the deal of the century" as it claimed.
